proofs.proof_tex:
By \texttt{def:target}, and using the existence of the displayed conditional expectations,
\[
\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}(1)\mid z_0]-\mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]\right\}.
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} gives \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely, hence equality of their conditional expectations.  Assumption \texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives
\(\mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]=m_s(z_{0s})\).  Substitution in the preceding finite sum yields
\[
\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\left\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\right\}.
\]
No regression, modulus, or sampling assertion is used in this equality.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{st})_{s,t})\), let \(\mathcal Z=\sigma((Z_j)_{j=1}^{N})\), and let \(\mathcal U\) be the sigma-field generated jointly by all untreated responses and event outcomes.  By \texttt{ass:donor-training-separation}, conditional on \(z_0\), \(\mathcal Z\) is independent of \(\mathcal X\vee\mathcal U\).  Consequently, for measurable sets \(A\in\mathcal Z\) and \(D\in\mathcal U\), a regular conditional kernel satisfies
\[
 P(A\cap D\mid z_0,\mathcal X)
 =P(A\mid z_0)P(D\mid z_0,\mathcal X).
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-independence} further makes the first factor the product of the \(N\) one-donor kernels.  Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} makes the second factor a product over the joint within-unit histories; it does not split a within-unit history into a pre-event response factor and an event-outcome factor.  Finally, \texttt{ass:center-only-design} says that \(X_{st}\) itself, rather than a noisy surrogate, is present in \(\mathcal X\).  Thus conditioning the response kernel on \(\mathcal X\) requires no integration against a measurement-error kernel and no deconvolution operator.

The omitted stronger factorization is not implied.  For example, retain any bounded regression satisfying the class restrictions, fix a constant \(b_s\), take independent Rademacher variables \(U_i\) across units, put \(Q_{s1i}=m_s(X_{s1})+\varepsilon U_i\), use fresh independent centered bounded errors in the other windows, and put \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=b_s+\varepsilon U_i\), with \(\varepsilon>0\) small enough to preserve the support bound.  Conditional on the design, different unit histories are independent, and the pre-event calendar array can be independent over time, but \(Q_{s1i}\) and \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\) are dependent within unit \(i\).  Hence the joint response--event kernel cannot in general be written as the product of a replicated-regression kernel and a treated-mean kernel.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\), and a feasible \(u=(u_1^{\top},\ldots,u_S^{\top})^{\top}\) satisfying \(\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2\le\delta\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity} gives
\[
 \|u\|_2^2
 \le \lambda_{\max}(\Sigma)\|\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2^2
 \le C_\Sigma\delta^2.
\]
The definition of the isotropic Holder ball in \texttt{ass:holder-regression} implies, for a constant \(C_H'\) depending only on \(L,d,\lambda\),
\[
 |m_s(x+v)-m_s(x)|\le C_H'\|v\|_2^{\kappa},
 \qquad \kappa=\min\{\lambda,1\},
\]
whenever \(x,x+v\in[0,1]^d\).  (For \(0<\lambda\le1\) this is the defining Holder inequality; for \(\lambda>1\), the first derivatives are uniformly bounded and the line-segment fundamental theorem of calculus gives the Lipschitz inequality.)  Since \(\pi_s>0\), \(\sum_s\pi_s=1\), and \(\|u_s\|_2\le\|u\|_2\),
\[
 \left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
 \le C_H'\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\|u_s\|_2^\kappa
 \le C_H'C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Taking the supremum over the feasible perturbations in \texttt{def:local-modulus} proves the upper bound with \(C=C_H'C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\).  The lower bound is precisely \texttt{ass:attainable-local-modulus}.  Combining the two inequalities proves the claim.

The cube \(\mathcal C=([0,1]^d)^S\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.  Its coordinatewise clipping map is its Euclidean metric projection, hence is continuous, Borel measurable, and nonexpansive.  Because \(z_0\in\mathcal C\),
\[
 \|\widetilde z_\ell-z_0\|_2
 =\|\Pi_{\mathcal C}(\overline Z_\ell)-\Pi_{\mathcal C}(z_0)\|_2
 \le \|\overline Z_\ell-z_0\|_2.
\]
The eigenvalue inequalities in \texttt{ass:donor-ellipticity} imply, for every vector \(v\),
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}v\|_2\le c_\Sigma^{-1/2}\|v\|_2,
 \qquad
 \|v\|_2\le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\|\Sigma^{-1/2}v\|_2.
\]
Applying these successively, with the preceding Euclidean contraction between them, gives
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\widetilde z_\ell-z_0)\|_2
 \le (C_\Sigma/c_\Sigma)^{1/2}
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}(\overline Z_\ell-z_0)\|_2.
\]

Since \(0<b_{0s}\le1\), the integer \(M_s=\lfloor\log_2(b_{0s}^{-1})\rfloor\) is nonnegative.  Thus \(\mathcal B_s=\{2^{-m}:0\le m\le M_s\}\) is finite, contains \(1\), and every member is at least \(b_{0s}\).  Eigenvalues are continuous functions of the entries of a symmetric matrix, so comparison with \(c_G\), deterministic first-element selection on a finite grid, and the stated fallback are Borel operations.  On a coercive candidate, \(\lambda_{\min}(G_{sT})\ge c_G>0\), so the Gram matrix is invertible and the local-polynomial intercept is unique.  A finite sample mean, clipping to \([-B,B]\), and averaging over finitely many donor folds are measurable; the fallback is therefore measurable as well.  Spectral clipping of a finite symmetric matrix is Borel, and all remaining finite sums, comparisons, and interval intersections in \texttt{def:honest-interval} are Borel on their declared branches.  The explicit bookkeeping branches cover every zero denominator, empty fold, failed inverse, nonfinite numerical input, and small-sample case, so no map remains undefined.

Each treated sample mean and each clipped fitted or fallback regression value belongs to \([-B,B]\).  Positivity and normalization of the cohort weights therefore give
\[
 \widehat\tau=\sum_s\pi_s(\overline B_s^{\mathrm{obs}}-\widehat m_s)\in[-2B,2B].
\]
The two displayed alternatives for \(C_\alpha\) now follow directly from \texttt{def:honest-interval}: the radius interval intersected with \([-2B,2B]\) is used on the regular branch, and the full range \([-2B,2B]\) is used on every declared bad branch.

Apply \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}.  On every design array in the positive-probability rectangle \(\mathcal D_n\), the lemma gives \(g_{1T}(z_0)<1\), \(R_D=n^{-1}\to0\), and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_t)]
 \ge {\Delta^2\over4}+o(1).
\]
For any fixed finite \(C\), the right side of the claimed estimator upper bound, \(CR_D=C/n\), tends to zero.  Thus that upper bound is false.  Since it is one inequality in the asserted three-sided chain, the claimed conditional frontier is false as stated.  The witness satisfies all frozen class conditions; the missing premise is a restriction such as \(E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0,(X_{uv})]=\mu_{1s}(z_0)\), which is not present in the frozen core and is not used here as an assumption.

The two laws in \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} belong to the same frozen class and have target separation \(\Delta>0\) and total variation distance \(q<1\).  The lemma's explicitly derived two-point inequality gives
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\tau}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}}
 \mathbb E_P[(\widetilde\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0]
 \ge {\Delta^2\over8}(1-q)>0.
\]
Along \(T=n_1=n\) and \(N=n^3\), direct substitution into \texttt{def:marginal-rate} gives \(R_\star=n^{-1}\to0\).  A positive constant cannot be asymptotically equivalent to \(R_\star\), proving the negative claim.  Algebraically, the labels obtained by comparing the four entries of the defined maximum remain valid descriptions of that formula; the formula is not the minimax risk over the frozen class.

Let \(I_n\) be any interval sequence with the coverage required in the original claim.  The common-submeasure calculation in \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction} yields
\[
 \liminf_n\max_{v\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_v}[\operatorname{length}(I_n)\mid z_0]
 \ge\Delta(1-2\alpha-q)>0.
\]
The same lemma gives \(R_\star^{1/2}=n^{-1/2}\to0\).  Therefore no interval, including \(C_\alpha\), can have both the asserted uniform coverage and expected length bounded by \(CR_\star^{1/2}\) over the frozen class.  This refutes the conjunction in the original theorem without making any claim about which of its two properties the particular studentized interval loses first.

theorem.statement: Under the frozen class \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the answer to \texttt{oeq:sharp-phase-intersections} is negative.  For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), there is a scalar submodel and a growth array with \(R_\star\to0\) for which every interval having asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly on that submodel has worst-case expected length bounded away from zero.  Hence no total feasible interval can attain a finite exact asymptotic minimax constant times \(R_\star^{1/2}\), at phase intersections or elsewhere, until the model excludes unrestricted event-outcome dependence on the realized training design.
theorem.proof_tex:
Use the two-law scalar submodel in \texttt{lem:common-design-shock-obstruction}, choosing \(q<1-2\alpha\).  The lemma proves both
\[
 R_\star^{1/2}=n^{-1/2}\longrightarrow0
\]
and, for every interval sequence with the stated uniform asymptotic coverage,
\[
 \liminf_n\sup_{P\in\{P_0,P_1\}}
 \mathbb E_P[\operatorname{length}(I_n)\mid z_0]
 \ge\Delta(1-2\alpha-q)>0.
\]
If an interval attained a finite exact constant \(K\) times \(R_\star^{1/2}\), its worst-case expected length would converge to zero, contradicting the second display.  The contradiction applies independently of covariance or long-run-variance estimation, so the product-experiment ordered-modulus handle cannot repair it within the current class.

added_lemmas.statement: For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), there are admissible fixed class parameters, a scalar specialization \(S=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), \(z_0=1/2\), \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), a number \(q\in(0,1-2\alpha)\), and two laws \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) with the following properties.  Their training and donor laws agree, their targets are separated by a constant \(\Delta=\tau_{P_1}(z_0)-\tau_{P_0}(z_0)>0\), and their observed-data laws agree on an event of probability \(1-q\) and have total variation distance \(q\).  Along \(T=n_1\to\infty\) and \(N=n_1^3\), one has \(R_\star\to0\), but the minimax mean squared error is bounded below by a positive constant and every sequence of intervals with asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under both laws has expected length bounded below by a positive constant.  Moreover, there are positive-probability exact-design rectangles on which \(g_{1T}(z_0)<1\), \(R_D\to0\), and the conditional squared error of \(\widehat\tau\) under \(P_1\) is bounded away from zero.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
It suffices to construct one admissible choice of the fixed class parameters, because the disputed assertions are stated without the missing event--design centering restriction.  Take \(S=1\), \(\pi_1=1\), \(H=0\), \(p=d=1\), \(z_0=1/2\), and \(\lambda=\kappa=1\), with \(r=0\) under the stated integer-order reduction.  Choose \(0<q<\min\{1/4,1-2\alpha\}\), \(b_*>0\), and \(a>0\) small enough for the wealth and Holder radii and large enough that \(a\ge c_{\mathrm{mod}}\).  These inequalities are compatible for an admissible nonempty choice of fixed constants.  Use the box kernel \(K(v)=\mathbf 1\{|v|\le1/2\}\), which satisfies the stated kernel conditions, and put
\[
 m(x)=a|x-z_0|,
 \qquad X_t\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\operatorname{Unif}[0,1],
 \qquad Q_{ti}=m(X_t).
\]
Let donor scores be \(Z_j=z_0+\xi_j\), where the \(\xi_j\) are independent Rademacher variables independent of the entire panel.  Then \(\Sigma=1\), the standardized fourth moment equals \(1\), and donor unbiasedness, ellipticity, and donor separation hold.  Let
\[
 E=\{X_1\le q\}.
\]
Under both laws set \(B_i(0)=0\).  Under \(P_0\), set \(B_i(1)=0\); under \(P_1\), set \(B_i(1)=b_*\mathbf 1_E\), identically for every \(i\), and in each case set \(B_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_i(1)\).

We verify membership rather than importing it into the construction.  Consistency holds by the last assignment.  Since \(m(z_0)=0\), event-date transport holds because \(B_i(0)=0\).  Taking \(a\) and \(b_*\) within the displayed support envelope gives bounded wealth.  The function \(m\) is Lipschitz with constant \(a\), and \(z_0\) is interior.  The design density equals one.  Conditional on the whole design, every unit history is deterministic; a product of identical point masses is the joint point mass, so the unit histories are conditionally independent even though their unconditional event outcomes share \(E\).  The training sequence \((X_t,(Q_{ti})_i)\) is independent over \(t\), hence has \(\beta(k)=0\) for every \(k\ge1\).  Training coordinates are observed exactly.  The donor assertions were verified above.  Finally, for \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\le1/2\),
\[
 \omega_P(\delta;z_0)
 =\sup_{|u|\le\delta}|a|u|-0|
 =a\delta
 \ge c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta.
\]
Thus both laws belong to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\).

By \texttt{def:target},
\[
 \tau_{P_0}(z_0)=0,
 \qquad
 \tau_{P_1}(z_0)=b_*P(E)=b_*q=:\Delta>0.
\]
All observables under \(P_0\) and \(P_1\) coincide on \(E^c\), whose probability is \(1-q\).  On \(E\), their event-outcome vectors are respectively the all-zero and all-\(b_*\) vectors, so the restrictions there are mutually singular.  It follows directly from the definition of total variation that
\[
 \|P_1-P_0\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=q.
\]
For completeness, define the test \(\varphi=\mathbf 1\{|\widetilde\tau-\Delta|<|\widetilde\tau|\}\).  Whenever \(\varphi=1\) under \(P_0\), or \(\varphi=0\) under \(P_1\), the corresponding squared estimation error is at least \(\Delta^2/4\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{v\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_v}\{(\widetilde\tau-\tau_{P_v})^2\}
 \ge {\Delta^2\over8}\{P_0(\varphi=1)+P_1(\varphi=0)\}
 \ge {\Delta^2\over8}(1-q),
\]
where the last inequality follows by writing both probabilities against a common dominating measure and integrating the pointwise minimum of the two densities.  This is the elementary two-point testing inequality, derived here without an external theorem.

Now take \(T=n_1=:n\) and \(N=n^3\).  Substitution into \texttt{def:marginal-rate} gives
\[
 R_\star
 =n^{-1}\vee n^{-4/3}\vee n^{-2}\vee n^{-3}
 =n^{-1}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The preceding constant two-point lower bound proves the asserted failure of the marginal rate.

The same pair yields the length obstruction.  Let \(I_n\) be any data-measurable interval satisfying
\(P_v\{\tau_{P_v}(z_0)\in I_n\}\ge1-\alpha-o(1)\) for \(v=0,1\).  Let \(\nu\) be the common subprobability measure obtained by restricting either observed law to \(E^c\), so \(\nu(\Omega)=1-q\).  Since the part over \(E\) has mass at most \(q\),
\[
 \nu\{0\in I_n\}\ge1-\alpha-q-o(1),
 \qquad
 \nu\{\Delta\in I_n\}\ge1-\alpha-q-o(1).
\]
The union bound within the measure \(\nu\) therefore gives
\[
 \nu\{0,\Delta\in I_n\}
 \ge1-2\alpha-q-o(1).
\]
On this event \(\operatorname{length}(I_n)\ge\Delta\), and the coefficient is positive by the choice of \(q\).  Thus
\[
 \liminf_n\max_{v\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{P_v}[\operatorname{length}(I_n)]
 \ge\Delta(1-2\alpha-q)>0.
\]

It remains to verify the conditional assertion about the displayed estimator.  Let \(\eta_n=n^{-2}\), and condition on any exact design array in the positive-probability rectangle
\[
 \mathcal D_n=\{z_0+\eta_n<X_t<z_0+2\eta_n\text{ for every }t\}.
\]
Because \(z_0>q\), \(\mathcal D_n\subset E^c\).  For every \(u\) with \(|u-z_0|\le N^{-1/2}=n^{-3/2}\), choose \(b_n=4(n^{-3/2}+2\eta_n)\).  On \(\mathcal D_n\), \(|X_t-u|/b_n\le1/4\), so the box kernel equals one and, because \(r=0\),
\[
 G_T(u,b_n)=b_n^{-1}\ge c_G
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).  Therefore \(g_{1T}(z_0)\le b_n<1\).  The bandwidth in \texttt{def:conditional-rate} satisfies
\[
 h_1^\star\asymp (Tn_1)^{-1/3}=n^{-2/3},
 \qquad
 R_D=n^{-1}\vee O(n^{-4/3})\vee n^{-3}=n^{-1}.
\]
Let \(b_{01}=n^{-2/3}\), and let \(A_n\) be the event that both projected donor-fold means lie within \(b_{01}/4\) of \(z_0\).  Projection is nonexpansive, each balanced raw fold mean has variance at most \(2/N\), and Markov's inequality applied to its square gives
\[
 P(A_n^c\mid z_0,\mathcal D_n)
 \le {64\over N b_{01}^2}=64n^{-5/3}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The smallest dyadic grid point lies in \([b_{01},2b_{01})\).  On \(A_n\cap\mathcal D_n\), every normalized design displacement at that bandwidth has absolute value below \(1/2\), so this first grid point is coercive.  The order-zero fitted value is a convex average of the \(Q_{ti}=m(X_t)\), and consequently
\[
 0\le\widehat m_1\le2a\eta_n.
\]
On \(E^c\), the observed treated mean is zero under both laws.  Hence \(|\widehat\tau|\le2a\eta_n\), whereas under \(P_1\), \(\tau(z_0)=\Delta\).  For all large \(n\), on \(A_n\),
\[
 |\widehat\tau-\tau_{P_1}(z_0)|\ge\Delta/2.
\]
It follows that, for every design array in \(\mathcal D_n\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_1}[(\widehat\tau-\tau_{P_1}(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_t)]
 \ge {\Delta^2\over4}P(A_n\mid z_0,(X_t))
 \longrightarrow {\Delta^2\over4},
\]
while \(R_D=n^{-1}\to0\).  This completes every part of the obstruction.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Conditional on \(z_0\) and the exact path-design array, the donor experiment is independent of the joint training-response and treated-event experiment, and its conditional kernel is the product of the \(N\) one-donor kernels. The remaining conditional kernel factors across joint within-unit histories, but need not factor between pre-event responses and treated event outcomes. Because every \(X_{st}\) is observed exactly, no convolution operator acts on a training coordinate.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen assumptions permit dependence between a unit's pre-event responses and its event outcome. Conditional cross-unit independence factors joint unit histories only, so the original three-experiment product claim is too strong. The donor separation and no-deconvolution conclusions remain valid.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The claimed conditional frontier does not hold over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) as currently defined. There are admissible fixed class parameters, a scalar specialization, a growth array, two laws in the class, and positive-probability exact-design rectangles on which \(g_{1T}(z_0)<1\) and \(R_D\to0\), but \(\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_t)]\) is bounded away from zero under one law. Hence no fixed finite \(C\) can satisfy the displayed upper bound for \(\widehat\tau\), and the three-sided frontier is false without an event-outcome conditional-centering restriction relative to the realized design.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The class controls event means only conditional on \(z_0\), while the theorem conditions risk on the whole training design. A treated event outcome may therefore contain a bounded common design shock. Conditional on the design, replicated units are independent because they are degenerate, yet the shock does not average out. The explicit two-law witness proves a constant conditional error while \(R_D\to0\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The claimed marginal minimax equivalence does not hold over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) as currently defined. There are two scalar laws in the class whose targets differ by a positive constant and whose observed-data total variation distance is a fixed number below one. Consequently the minimax mean squared error is bounded away from zero along a growth array for which \(R_\star\to0\). The oracle and generated-proxy labels remain algebraically valid descriptions of the entries of the defined maximum \(R_\star\), but that maximum is not the minimax frontier over the frozen class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The same allowed common design shock yields a two-point Le Cam obstruction after averaging over the random design. Replication does not remove it because all event outcomes may be the same design-measurable constant conditional on the design.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The claimed honest-length frontier does not hold over \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) as currently defined. For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), there is a scalar two-law submodel and a growth array with \(R_\star^{1/2}\to0\) such that every interval having asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under both laws has worst-case expected length bounded away from zero. Hence the displayed \(C_\alpha\) cannot simultaneously have the asserted uniform coverage and \(O(R_\star^{1/2})\) expected length on the frozen class.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: On an event of probability \(1-q\), the two observed laws coincide while their causal targets are separated by a constant. If \(q<1-2\alpha\), coverage under both laws forces any interval to contain both targets with positive probability on that common event, giving a constant expected-length lower bound.

There are admissible fixed class parameters, a scalar specialization, a growth array, two laws in the class, and positive-probability exact-design rectangles on which \(g_{1T}(z_0)<1\) and \(R_D\to0\), but \(\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau-\tau(z_0))^2\mid z_0,(X_t)]\) is bounded away from zero under one law. Hence no fixed finite \(C\) can satisfy the displayed upper bound for \(\widehat\tau\), and the three-sided frontier is false without an event-outcome conditional-centering restriction relative to the realized design.

For every \(\alpha\in(0,1/2)\), there is a scalar two-law submodel and a growth array with \(R_\star^{1/2}\to0\) such that every interval having asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) under both laws has worst-case expected length bounded away from zero. proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\). This observed-law identity follows from consistency and event-date transport. Over the frozen class, no MSE equivalence to \(R_\star\) follows because treated event outcomes need not be conditionally centered given the realized training design.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The existing metadata advertises the refuted \(R_\star\) minimax equivalence. The causal identifying equality remains valid and must be kept distinct from the invalid rate claim.

proofs.proof_tex:
Put \(a_0=\min\{B,L,1\}/64\), let \(q_0=(\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e)^{1/2}\), and condition throughout on the fixed value of \(z_0\).  Both constants are strictly positive.  We verify the defining conditions of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) one at a time.

First consider the causal outcome construction.  At the event location \(z_{0s}=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_d\), both displayed alternatives for \(m_1\) equal \(4a_0\), and the same is true for every \(m_s\) with \(s>1\).  Hence
\[
 B_{si}(0)\in\{3a_0,5a_0\},\qquad
 B_{si}(1)\in\{4a_0,6a_0\}.
\]
In particular, these potential wealth levels are positive.  The prescribed returns therefore satisfy \(R_{si0}(a)=B_{si}(a)-1>-1\), and, because \(W_{si,-1}=1\) and \(R_{sih}(a)=0\) for \(h>0\),
\[
 W_{si,-1}\prod_{h=0}^{H}\{1+R_{sih}(a)\}
 =1\cdot B_{si}(a)\prod_{h=1}^{H}1
 =B_{si}(a).
\]
Thus the prescribed returns generate the prescribed buy-and-hold levels.  The equality \(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) gives consistency.  Since \(\eta_{si}\) is centered and independent of \(z_0\),
\[
 \mathbb E[B_{si}(0)\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s})+a_0\mathbb E[\eta_{si}\mid z_0]
 =m_s(z_{0s}),
\]
which gives event-date transport.  Each outcome depends only on its own unit and the indicated path, so the construction has neither spillovers nor dependence on future treatment.

We next check support and the regression condition.  If \(\kappa=1\), writing \(y=x_1-1/2\in[-1/2,1/2]\) gives \(-1/4\le y+y^2\le3/4\), and hence
\[
 15a_0/4\le m_1(x)\le19a_0/4.
\]
If \(0<\kappa<1\), the positive and negative parts cannot both be nonzero and
\[
 7a_0/2\le m_1(x)\le5a_0.
\]
For \(s>1\), \(m_s(x)=4a_0\).  Consequently, in all cases,
\[
 |Q_{sti}|\vee|B_{si}(0)|\vee|B_{si}(1)|
 \le 6a_0\le 6B/64<B,
\]
so bounded wealth holds.  Conditional centering of \(\varepsilon_{sti}\) yields, for every \(s,t,i\),
\[
 \mathbb E[Q_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]
 =m_s(x)+a_0\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{sti}\mid X_{st}=x]
 =m_s(x),
\]
and the right side does not depend on \(t\).  The conditional response variance is \(a_0^2>0\), and the conditional variance of each event potential wealth level is also \(a_0^2>0\).

The displayed surfaces are in the required isotropic Holder ball.  Indeed, when \(0<\lambda=\kappa<1\), the elementary inequality
\[
 |r_+^{\lambda}-q_+^{\lambda}|\le |r-q|^{\lambda}
\]
implies that the Holder seminorm of the nonconstant part of \(m_1\) is at most \(3a_0/2\); together with the preceding supremum bound, its usual isotropic Holder norm is less than \(7a_0\).  When \(\lambda\ge1\), \(\kappa=1\) and the nonzero derivatives of \(m_1\) are
\[
 \partial_1m_1(x)=a_0\{1+2(x_1-1/2)\},
 \qquad \partial_{11}m_1(x)=2a_0.
\]
Their suprema are at most \(2a_0\); all derivatives of order greater than two vanish, and the first derivative is Lipschitz with constant \(2a_0\).  Thus, for every \(\lambda\ge1\), the defining derivative suprema and terminal fractional seminorm in the isotropic Holder norm sum to less than \(9a_0\).  The constant surfaces have norm \(4a_0\).  Since \(9a_0<64a_0\le L\), every \(m_s\) belongs to \(\mathcal H_d(\lambda,L)\).

The design variables are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\), so their common density is \(f_X(x)=1\).  The declared bounds \(c_X\le1\le C_X\) therefore give the design-density condition.  Moreover,
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(z_{0s},\partial[0,1]^d)=1/2\ge\delta_0,
\]
so the event path is interior.  Independence over calendar windows implies that every beta-mixing coefficient at a positive lag is zero, whence \(\beta(k)=0\le\beta_0\rho_0^k\).  Conditional on the path-design array and \(z_0\), the mutually independent noises \((\varepsilon_{sti},\eta_{si})\) give independence across \((s,i)\).  The paths \(X_{st}\) are observed directly, as required by the center-only design condition.  Finally, the stipulated mutual independence of the Rademacher noises, the training variables, and the event noises gives donor-training separation.

It remains to verify the donor conditions.  Because the coordinates of \(U_j\) are independent centered Rademacher variables,
\[
 \mathbb E[Z_j\mid z_0]=z_0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(Z_j\mid z_0)
 =\Sigma^{1/2}I_{Sd}\Sigma^{1/2}=\Sigma.
\]
The \(Z_j\)'s are conditionally independent and identically distributed.  For
\[
 \Sigma=\frac12I_{Sd}+\frac{1}{2Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}\mathbf 1_{Sd}^{\top},
\]
the vector \(\mathbf 1_{Sd}\) has eigenvalue \(1\), while every vector orthogonal to it has eigenvalue \(1/2\).  Hence
\[
 c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}
\]
under the displayed restrictions \(c_\Sigma\le1/2\) and \(C_\Sigma\ge1\).  The covariance is positive definite, and each of its off-diagonal entries equals \(1/(2Sd)>0\).  Moreover,
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\|\Sigma^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\mid z_0\right]
 =\mathbb E[\|U_j\|_2^4]
 =(Sd)^2\le B^4.
\]
This proves unbiasedness, ellipticity, and the required fourth-moment bound.

We finally prove the attainable local modulus rather than assuming it from smoothness.  Since \(q_0>0\), for every \(0<\delta\le\delta_0\) define
\[
 u_\delta=\delta\Sigma\bar e/q_0.
\]
Then
\[
 \|\Sigma^{-1/2}u_\delta\|_2^2
 =\frac{\delta^2}{q_0^2}\bar e^{\top}\Sigma\bar e
 =\delta^2,
 \qquad
 \bar e^{\top}u_\delta
 =\delta q_0>0.
\]
The restriction on \(\delta_0\) also gives
\[
 \|u_\delta\|_\infty
 \le\delta_0\|\Sigma\bar e/q_0\|_\infty
 \le1/2.
\]
Because \(z_0=\tfrac12\mathbf 1_{Sd}\), this proves \(z_0+u_\delta\in([0,1]^d)^S\), so \(u_\delta\) is feasible in the supremum defining \(\omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}\).

Only the first coordinate of the first cohort contributes to the weighted surface increment.  If \(\kappa=1\), the gradient of the stacked weighted surface at \(z_0\) is \(\pi_1a_0\bar e\); its covariance-standardized norm is
\[
 \|\Sigma^{1/2}(\pi_1a_0\bar e)\|_2
 =\pi_1a_0q_0>0.
\]
Direct substitution also gives
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0(q_0\delta+q_0^2\delta^2)
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0}{64}\delta+O(\delta^2).
\]
In particular, this increment is at least \(\pi_1a_0q_0\delta\).  If \(0<\kappa<1\), positivity of \(\bar e^{\top}u_\delta\) instead gives the exact identity
\[
 \sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_{\delta,s})-m_s(z_{0s})\}
 =\pi_1a_0q_0^{\kappa}\delta^{\kappa}
 =\frac{\pi_1\min\{B,L,1\}q_0^{\kappa}}{64}\delta^{\kappa}.
\]
Thus in either case, using the displayed choice
\(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\le\pi_1a_0\min\{q_0,q_0^\kappa\}\),
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)
 \ge c_{\mathrm{mod}}\delta^\kappa
 \qquad(0<\delta\le\delta_0).
\]
This is precisely the maintained attainable-direction condition.

For completeness, Holder regularity also supplies the matching upper order.  For every feasible \(u\), ellipticity implies
\[
 \|u\|_2=\|\Sigma^{1/2}\Sigma^{-1/2}u\|_2
 \le C_\Sigma^{1/2}\delta.
\]
Let \(C_{\mathrm{Hol}}<\infty\) denote the fixed norm-equivalence constant in the Holder increment bound (the Lipschitz bound when \(\lambda\ge1\)).  For all sufficiently small \(\delta\), that bound gives
\[
 \left|\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{m_s(z_{0s}+u_s)-m_s(z_{0s})\}\right|
 \le C_{\mathrm{Hol}}L\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\|u_s\|_2^\kappa
 \le C_{\mathrm{Hol}}L C_\Sigma^{\kappa/2}\delta^\kappa.
\]
Here \(C_{\mathrm{Hol}}\) depends only on the fixed Holder-norm convention and \(d\).  Taking the supremum and combining this upper bound with the preceding feasible-direction lower bound proves
\[
 \omega_{P_{\mathrm{ex}}}(\delta;z_0)\asymp\delta^\kappa
 \qquad\text{as }\delta\downarrow0.
\]
All defining conditions of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) have now been checked.  Hence \(P_{\mathrm{ex}}\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), with bounded nonzero response noise, an interior design point, and the asserted full non-diagonal positive-definite donor covariance.  The argument establishes membership for this explicit law only; it does not infer the lower modulus for an arbitrary Holder surface.
